title: de.hubtask.work.container.restored.v1
description: A container's deletion has been reversed, whole. Distinct from unarchived for the reason given there: a rule written to react to something coming back from a deletion must not fire when somebody unarchives a hub. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: A snapshot of the container as it now stands, deleted_at null again, with how much came back.

parent_id.description: The hub a collection sits in; null for a hub (invariant I-C1).

color_token.description: A theme token rather than a colour value, so that a client can render it in its own palette.

order_key.description: The rank among the siblings: a fractional index, not a number (offline-sync.md §4.2).

completion_policy.description: Whether a child's completion propagates upwards (invariant I-W5). Meaningful on a collection; a hub holds no items and reports the default.

archived_at.description: When this container was archived in its own right. Null for a collection that is only read-only because its hub is - effective_archived is the one to read for that.

effective_archived.description: Whether the container is read-only: archived itself, or sitting in an archived hub (invariant I-C3). Not derivable from this payload's other fields, which is why it is here.

deleted_at.description: When the entry went into the trash. Null when it is not in it. A soft delete with a retention period running against it, not a removal - the entry is still there and can be restored (ADR-0020).

trash_batch_id.description: The deletion every row of one act shares (invariant I-C2). It is what a restore is keyed on, and what tells a consumer that this entry went with something else rather than on its own. Null when the entry is not in the trash.

collections.description: How many collections the act took with it. Zero for a collection, which holds none.

items.description: How many entries the act took with it, at every level. A consumer cannot derive it - nothing below the container gets an event of its own - and an event whose size grew with the subtree would eventually be one nobody can deliver.
